events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The driver cancelled and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged, so the case enters through NS-0's driver-cancellation-with-no-show branch: NS-1 / NS-2 apply [F4][F8][NS-0]. The rider's complaint is that the driver was not at the pin ("at the entrance") [F11], which goes to NS-1 (ii) — whether the driver was at the pick-up point according to GPS when he pressed "I'm Here" [F6][NS-1].

System records control over statements where they conflict. The timeline shows the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:07:40 while 181 m from the pickup point, and the GPS shows he had entered the 200 m radius at 14:06:40 and stayed inside it until cancelling at 14:11:20 [F1][F2][F3][F5][F6]. His closest approach was 60 m [F1]. Because the 200 m radius is the data-layer definition of "at the pick-up location" used to check NS-1 (ii), a 181 m position at the moment of the tap satisfies that condition [F1][F6][NS-1]; the rider's subjective expectation that the car be exactly at the entrance pin does not defeat the GPS-based test.

NS-1 (iii) is also met: within 200 m before cancellation the cumulative time was 4 min 40 s, and after the tap the driver remained continuously inside the radius for 3 min 40 s (220 s), both exceeding the 3-minute threshold [F2][F6][NS-1]. Waiting time after the tap is corroborated by the driver's own message at 14:11 stating he had waited more than 3 minutes before cancelling [F12], which is consistent with the GPS timeline rather than contradicted by it.

The rider's side of the encounter is recorded too — at 14:09 she said she was at the entrance and could not see him [F11] — but on a completed no-show sequence where all three NS-1 conditions hold, that does not shift the fee: NS-1 makes the $6.61 cancellation fee (of which $4.50 goes to the driver) valid, i.e. no_action [F11][NS-1]. No traffic or weather facts are relied on here, as route deviation is not in issue [F14][F15][F16].

There is a record conflict between the timeline, which shows a tap at 14:07:40, and the separate timeline entry recording a null tap [F6][F7]. Under the rule that platform-recorded timeline/GPS entries govern and that the arrival confirmation is satisfied when the driver tapped "I'm Here" or the platform auto-confirmed arrival, the trace credit for NS-1 (i) stands on the 14:07:40 arrival record [F5][F6][NS-1]; the null entry is treated as an artifact and, on these facts, does not by itself establish an abuse of the "I'm Here" button that would trigger NS-2's flag [F6][F7][F3][NS-2].

No unexempted detour segment exists (no gps-detour facts), so RD-2 does not produce any refund and RD-6's precondition (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) is not met [F14][F15][RD-2][RD-6]. The profile fields are not used to decide the merits; the driver's two upheld no-show disputes over 90 days do not create an account action in this case since the clause trigger is absent [F17][F18][RD-6].
